Subject: Mutual Action Plan & Stakeholder Map — FinPay next steps

Thanks for the call today — appreciate the walkthrough of Redwood's runtime and the potential latency/cost improvements for our user lookup pipeline. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can get the internal roadmap aligned:

- Decision criteria we care about: latency under 120ms p95, predictable token cost, SOC2 compliance, and a clear rollout path for Canary -> Prod.
- Primary use case: real-time enrichment during fraud checks (low latency, high QPS).
- Internal stakeholders I need to align: myself (A. Li, Product), Priya Sharma (Procurement), Daniel Park (Finance), Naveen Gupta (Security).

Can you share a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and a stakeholder map we can circulate? Also flag any documents you need from our side (e.g., SOC2, encryption details, network topology).

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to share MAP + stakeholder map (Marissa)
2) We’ll confirm procurement steps and timeline (Priya)
3) Schedule a short technical demo for our infra team (Connor or equivalent)

Thanks — happy to sync quickly if helpful.

— Aaron
Aaron Li
Head of Product, FinPay

Hi Marissa/Aaron — thanks for sending the MAP. Quick note on procurement steps from our side (FinPay):

1) Standard onboarding docs: Supplier questionnaire, W-9 (US), vendor master form.
2) Security evidence: SOC2 report or similar, encryption at rest details, data residency notes. Send to Naveen (security) for review.
3) Contract: we use our PO process — procurement sends PO after commercial terms & SOW are agreed.
4) Timeline: typical procurement window is 3–4 weeks after final SOW/contract; faster if we can do an internal approval by 2026-04-02.

Owners: Priya Sharma (procurement lead) — procurement@finpay.com; Daniel Park (Finance) — daniel.park@finpay.com; Olivia Chen (Legal) — olivia.chen@finpay.com.

If Redwood can provide SOC2 and a redline-friendly contract within the week, we’ll prioritize. Also please include estimated monthly spend for the pilot so Finance can provision a PO.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & Stakeholder Map — tech follow-ups

Aaron / team — quick technical follow-up after reviewing the use case and the MAP: 

- Integration pattern: server-side API calls with prefix caching and per-tenant KV cache to keep token usage predictable.
- Latency targets: we can meet 120ms p95 for enriched lookups with a small staging cluster; will need expected QPS numbers and average sequence length to size correctly.
- Security: we recommend private VPC peering for the pilot or a dedicated instance depending on data sensitivity. If VPC peering is not possible, IP allowlist + mTLS is workable.
- Demo: I can run a 30-minute demo showing request flow, batching behavior, and cost telemetry if the FinPay infra team can join. Suggested slots: 3/23 10:00–10:30 PST or 3/24 14:00–14:30 PST.

Aaron — could you confirm QPS and sample payload sizes so we can finalize the staging spec? Also tagging Naveen for any security constraints we should pre-empt.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
